title: Material library | Mr Wallcover
description: Paper, grasscloth, silk, hand-painted scenics, murals, contract vinyl and acoustic wallcoverings. Installation and sourcing; physical samples decide colour.
heading: Find the right wallcovering for your room.
lede: Seven material families: paper, grasscloth, silk and textiles, hand-painted scenics, murals, contract vinyl and acoustic wallcoverings, with what each one asks of the wall, the joins and the cleaning. We hang all of them and can source them when you want that. A screen cannot show colour, texture or sheen, so order a physical sample before you decide.

items.name: Paper and non-woven
items.metaTitle: Paper and non-woven wallpaper installation | Mr Wallcover
items.appearance: Printed or plain, from a quiet texture to a large repeat.
items.metaDescription: Paper and non-woven wallcoverings, printed or plain, from a quiet texture to a large repeat, surveyed and hung by Mr Wallcover in London.
items.joins: Seams are part of a hung wall. The match follows the repeat: free or straight. Half-drop and murals are set out on site, not by the simple calculator.
items.care: Follow the maker. Many papers are not washable. We do not call a family washable, fire-rated or seamless unless that product’s own data says so.
items.handling: The wall has to be sound first. Lining is used when the maker or the wall requires it.

decision.considerWhen: You want a printed pattern or a quieter, more even visual finish.
decision.tradeoff: Print, backing and care vary substantially between products.
decision.checkBeforeOrdering: Confirm the repeat, match, usable width and actual cleaning instructions.

evidence.caption: Printed Adam’s Eden by Adam Calkin for Lewis & Wood at Brown’s Hotel, Mayfair, with its printed selvedge still visible. The repeat and edge are product-specific.

items.name: Grasscloth and natural weaves
items.metaTitle: Grasscloth and natural weave installation | Mr Wallcover
items.appearance: Sisal, raffia, grass and other weaves. Colour and texture move from roll to roll.
items.joins: Seams show. The direction of the weave is agreed before the first length is cut.
items.care: Dry and gentle. Adhesive on the face marks the weave. Not a washable surface.
items.handling: Clean hands, an adhesive that suits the backing, and enough length from one batch to keep a wall together.

decision.considerWhen: Natural fibre and a visible panel character are part of the look you want.
decision.tradeoff: Adjacent drops can differ in shade; do not expect an invisible joint.
decision.checkBeforeOrdering: Review a full-wall example, panel layout and the exact care sheet.

evidence.caption: A woven grasscloth turning an external corner at the Four Seasons residences, Ten Trinity Square. The close view shows the natural fibre and the finished edge.

items.name: Silk and textiles
items.metaTitle: Silk and textile wallcovering installation | Mr Wallcover
items.setting: Rooms where light is part of the finish
items.appearance: A cloth face with a sheen that changes as you move.
items.metaDescription: Silk and textile wallcoverings: a cloth face with a sheen that changes as you move, surveyed and hung by Mr Wallcover in London.
items.joins: Seams are planned so the light from the window does not catch a ridge.
items.care: Silk marks quickly. Care is the maker’s note, usually dry. It is not a corridor vinyl.
items.handling: Clean hands, the specified adhesive, and preparation written into the scope, including a lining where one is required.

decision.considerWhen: You want a textile surface whose appearance changes with the light.
decision.tradeoff: Delicate faces can be less forgiving of marks and handling.
decision.checkBeforeOrdering: See the sample in the room and confirm preparation and care requirements.

evidence.caption: Fromental hand-painted silk at Four Seasons Hotel London at Ten Trinity Square. Light picks out the marbled face; a physical sample in the room remains essential.

items.name: Hand-painted scenic papers
items.metaTitle: Hand-painted scenic wallpaper installation | Mr Wallcover
items.appearance: Scenic and panelled papers, in the manner of houses such as de Gournay and Fromental. We hang them. We do not make them, and we are not affiliated with those makers.
items.metaDescription: Scenic and panelled papers in the manner of de Gournay and Fromental. We hang them; we do not make them and are not affiliated with those makers.
items.joins: Panels follow a sequence. The scene has to meet across doors, windows and corners. The set-out starts from a fixed point.
items.care: As the maker specifies. These are not washable contract surfaces.
items.handling: A sound wall, time, and the maker’s instruction on lining.

decision.considerWhen: The scene should be designed around the room and its focal points.
decision.tradeoff: Doors, corners and furniture can interrupt the composition.
decision.checkBeforeOrdering: Agree elevations, panel sequence, supplier proof and finished dimensions.

evidence.caption: de Gournay hand-painted wallpaper installed in a private London residence, photographed under the room’s wall lights. The scene must be planned around these fixed fittings.

items.name: Murals
items.metaTitle: Mural wallpaper installation in London | Mr Wallcover
items.setting: A single wall or a room with a scene
items.appearance: Printed or hand-made scenes, including event murals hung for a fixed date.
items.joins: Set out from a fixed point so the image meets where it should. A roll calculator will not price a mural.
items.care: Follow the maker. An event mural is not the same duty as a guest-room vinyl.
items.handling: Check the panel count, the sequence and the substrate before the first piece is opened.

decision.considerWhen: One wall or a room needs a planned composition rather than a repeating pattern.
decision.tradeoff: A preview cannot confirm the real colour, texture or precise crop.
decision.checkBeforeOrdering: Confirm scale, panel count, sequence, backing and care instructions.

evidence.caption: A Calico Wallpaper landscape continues around an internal corner at Heathrow Terminal 4. The scene and the return were set out together before the store fixtures went in.

items.name: Contract vinyl
items.metaTitle: Contract vinyl wallcovering installation | Mr Wallcover
items.appearance: A tighter face specified for wear. At The OWO the install included Vescom.
items.joins: Seams are still there. They are planned, not promised away.
items.care: More tolerant of cleaning than paper or silk, and still only as the maker allows. Vinyl on a wall is not, by itself, a fire certificate.
items.handling: The specified adhesive, the right substrate, and a sample in the room’s own light when the specification is still open.

decision.considerWhen: Cleaning and everyday wear are priorities worth discussing with the supplier.
decision.tradeoff: The material name alone does not establish wet-area or fire suitability.
decision.checkBeforeOrdering: Check the particular product, cleaning method and project specification.

evidence.caption: A close view of the jet-black embossed Muraspec installed at Hilton London Metropole. Texture is visible here; cleaning and fire requirements still depend on the exact product documents.

items.name: Acoustic wallcoverings
items.metaTitle: Acoustic wallcovering installation in London | Mr Wallcover
items.setting: Rooms where sound was part of the specification
items.appearance: A textured face over an acoustic construction, or an acoustic panel.
items.metaDescription: Acoustic wallcoverings: a textured face over an acoustic construction, or an acoustic panel, surveyed and installed by Mr Wallcover in London.
items.joins: Edges, trims and cuts have to keep the system the way it was specified.
items.care: Follow the system maker. We do not claim a decorative finish is an acoustic rating.
items.handling: Adhesive, trimming and edges follow the instruction for that system. The material light studio does not show acoustic performance.

decision.considerWhen: Sound performance forms part of a professionally specified system.
decision.tradeoff: A decorative texture is not evidence of acoustic performance.
decision.checkBeforeOrdering: Obtain the exact system data, installation detail and project acceptance.

evidence.caption: Elitis wallcovering installed in a private cinema room in Mayfair. This records the face and the installation; acoustic performance is established by the exact system’s documents.
